$comment: ONE source of truth, read by the Python provisioner (installation/provisioner.py) and by the desktop payload staging, which shells out to it. Every entry pins an EXACT version plus, per target, the exact download URL and its sha256. No ranges, no 'resolve latest and hope': a build is reproducible, needs no GitHub API (unauthenticated callers get 60 requests/hour), and a tool cannot silently change under users. Bump deliberately: change the version, refresh every url+sha256 for that tool, verify, commit. Tool ORDER is derived from this file too — see 'extends'.

npm.$comment: Newer than the npm bundled inside the pinned node. 'extends' says both things that follow from that: install npm AFTER node (staging runs node's own npm to unpack this tarball), and put npm's bin dir BEFORE node's on PATH, or node's bundled npm shadows this one. The registry tarball is the same bytes for every target, so it pins one 'any' artifact; the per-target part is the shim layout npm writes on install, which _binary_rel owns.

git.$comment: Windows only. On Windows we need git bash, so the managed PortableGit is the contract rather than a preference. On macOS and Linux the machine's git is used when it clears the flag floor; see the per-target missing entries.

darwin-arm64.missing: not bundled by choice: a 147MB dugite download to run `git rev-parse` is the wrong trade where git is one package-manager command away. installation.git.git_path() takes a system git that clears the flag floor, and reports git_install_guidance() when there is none. Windows still bundles: bash.exe ships inside PortableGit and a system git's bash can be missing or ASLR-broken.

ripgrep.$comment: Fast file search behind search_files. Linux uses the musl build so it does not depend on the host glibc.

cua-driver.$comment: OPTIONAL: the Computer Use driver, a self-contained Rust binary that speaks MCP over stdio. The `-binary` release variants unpack flat (cua-driver, cua-cursor-theme, the SDK library, and on Windows the cua-driver-uia.exe UIAccess worker), so the binary runs straight out of its store entry with no installer state: no ~/.cua-driver home, no versioned-dirs + `current` symlink farm, no /Applications bundle. Both darwin targets take the same universal artifact, which carries an x86_64 and an arm64 slice. macOS NOTE: the upstream installer places CuaDriver.app in /Applications so TCC grants attribute to com.trycua.driver; a pinned binary has no bundle, so the driver runs with `mcp --direct` and the grants attribute to the host process instead (Hermes, or the terminal that spawned it). That is the deliberate trade for one code path on every platform. Telemetry is upstream-default-ON and is disabled through CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED (cua_backend.cua_driver_child_env), which the provisioner's version probe passes too, so provisioning never creates an installation id.

agent-browser.$comment: OPTIONAL: the browser driver, a self-contained Rust binary that speaks CDP. One registry tarball ships every platform's binary (68.5MB unpacked); the fact records the HOST's native binary directly, so no node/npm is needed to run it. Pinned exactly (0.26.0 is the only 0.26.x) so a sealed bundle resolves no floating range at runtime. win32-arm64 is a declared gap: the tarball and the v0.26.0 GitHub release both ship no ARM64 Windows binary. requires: a driver without a browser is not a configuration anyone wants -- selecting agent-browser selects the pinned Chromium pair with it (selection only; no PATH or ordering consequence).

win32-arm64.missing: agent-browser ships no win32-arm64 binary (absent from the npm tarball and the v0.26.0 release assets)

chromium.$comment: OPTIONAL: the Playwright chromium build (decision 13). Replaces the installers' `npx playwright install chromium` ladders: those fetch whatever revision the npm-resolved playwright wants, unverified, and hang on apt releases playwright does not recognize (#35166). The pin version IS playwright's chromium revision, and it must equal the revision in the root package-lock's playwright-core browsers.json (chromium 1208 = browserVersion 145.0.7632.6, playwright 1.58.2) -- enforced by tests/test_chromium_pin_lockstep.py: bump playwright and this pin in ONE commit or CI fails. x64/mac/win are Chrome-for-Testing zips on the bare cdn keyed by browserVersion; linux-arm64 is the classic revision path (playwright-core's own DOWNLOAD_PATHS split). No win32-arm64 build exists upstream -- that target keeps the system-browser rung. STORE LAYOUT EXCEPTION: playwright resolves browsers by directory name under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, so these entries are named playwright's way in the shared store (chromium-1208/, no target suffix -- store_entry_name special-cases it) and installation/env.py points PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH at the store root. No links (banned), no per-install copies. Archives keep their internal layout (chrome-linux64/chrome etc.), and the entry gets playwright's INSTALLATION_COMPLETE marker so its registry trusts the dir. Known hazard, accepted: a hand-run `npx playwright install` from a DIFFERENT playwright version may GC entries whose revision it does not expect; the facts detect the vanish and the next sweep reprovisions. onPath false: a browser tree is not a CLI surface.

win32-arm64.missing: no upstream build (neither CfT nor the classic playwright CDN ship windows-arm64); the target keeps the system-browser rung

chromium-headless-shell.$comment: OPTIONAL: chromium's headless companion. Playwright >=1.49 launches headless=True through chromium_headless_shell-<rev>, NOT the full chromium (playwright-core chromium.js:324), so a pin shipping only chromium would break every headless launch -- which is nearly all of them (doctor_live, google_meet, skills). Same revision lockstep, same store-naming exception, same missing win32-arm64 as chromium.

win32-arm64.missing: no upstream build (neither CfT nor the classic playwright CDN ship windows-arm64); the target keeps the system-browser rung

llamacpp-cuda.$comment: llama.cpp's CUDA build — the engine behind the managed local runtime (llama-server). Upstream numbers builds (rolling bNNNN tags) rather than releasing semver, so the version is the bare build number and the 'b' lives in the URL, the same shape as playwright's chromium revision. Optional: nobody downloads a 270MB inference engine until they ask for a local model. The cudart DLLs ride along in 'also' rather than as a tool of their own: Windows resolves a DLL from the loading executable's OWN directory, so they have to land beside llama-server.exe — a second entry plus a PATH edge would not be found. Bumping the build means refreshing both digests here, which is the point: the engine that runs a user's model is pinned like every other tool instead of resolved at runtime.

win32-x64.missing: only win32-arm64 is pinned so far. Upstream ships builds for the other targets (and macOS is a single unified tarball with Metal built in); add them by refreshing url+sha256 from the release, one target at a time.
